decision: Replace in-memory Map-backed JobStore with a PostgresJobStore (pg driver, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, single job table, available_at bigint, two partial indexes WHERE state IN CREATED/LOCKED). Promote InMemoryJobStore as explicit TestDouble; re-export it as JobStore alias so all 3 frozen unit-test files compile unchanged. Add available_at to Job TS interface (additive, no frozen test constructs Job literals). Ops ops run_vacuum/queue_stats as standalone Node/TS scripts in ops/catalog/. Health extends with queue.depth + oldestAvailableLagMs, backward-compatible. Zero breaking changes to public interface surface.

rejected_alternatives.option: Advisory locks instead of SKIP LOCKED
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Advisory locks require application-level lock ID management; SKIP LOCKED is purpose-built for queues and already mandated by ratified stack ADR §1.
inbox_task is an alias in current codebase, not a distinct entity. One table job with topic column covers all types; splitting would duplicate schema/index logic without behavioral justification.
NF-4 explicitly forbids ORM; zero-dep in domain logic is a stack invariant. Raw pg + parameterised SQL is proportional.
Changes client interaction model (push vs pull); the external-worker pull model is the current contract. Over-engineering without spec justification.

rejected_alternatives.option: available_at only in DB, not in Job TS interface
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Leaves TS Job diverged from DB row; getById would return partial view; breaks client code reading available_at. Additive field is the clean approach.
T-0114's goal is durability and concurrency correctness; in-memory loses data on restart and is unsafe for multi-worker concurrency.

contracts: fetchAndLock SQL: WITH candidates AS (SELECT id FROM job WHERE topic=ANY($topics) AND ((state='CREATED' AND available_at<=$now) OR (state='LOCKED' AND lock_expiry<=$now)) ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT $maxJobs FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) UPDATE job SET state='LOCKED', lock_owner=$workerId, lock_expiry=$now+$lockDurationMs FROM candidates WHERE job.id=candidates.id RETURNING job.*
complete SQL: single atomic CTE — read gate (NOT_FOUND|NOT_LOCKED|LOCK_EXPIRED|NOT_OWNER), UPDATE on verdict=OK, RETURNING verdict

fail SQL: same gate CTE; on OK: SET state=CASE WHEN retries>0 THEN 'CREATED' ELSE 'FAILED' END, retries=$r, lock_owner=NULL, lock_expiry=NULL, available_at=CASE WHEN retries>0 THEN $now+$retryTimeoutMs ELSE available_at END
Health query: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state='CREATED' AND available_at<=$now) AS depth, MIN(available_at) FILTER (WHERE state='CREATED' AND available_at<=$now) AS oldest FROM job

queue_stats query: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state IN ('CREATED','LOCKED') AND available_at<=$now) AS depth, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state='LOCKED') AS locked_count, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state='FAILED') AS failed_count, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state='COMPLETED') AS completed_count, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state='FAILED' AND retries=0) AS dlq_count, MIN(available_at) FILTER (...available...) AS oldest_available_at FROM job
src/core/jobStore.ts re-exports: export { InMemoryJobStore as JobStore }; export { PostgresJobStore }; export type { CompleteResult, FailResult, ErrorCode }

Migration 010_add_available_at_and_indexes.sql: ALTER TABLE job ADD COLUMN available_at bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; UPDATE job SET available_at=created_at WHERE available_at=0; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_job_fetchable_created ON job(tenant_id,topic,created_at) WHERE state='CREATED'; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_job_fetchable_locked ON job(tenant_id,topic,created_at) WHERE state='LOCKED'
run_vacuum: VACUUM ANALYZE job; returns JSON stdout; exit 0 always; DATABASE_URL from env or --db arg
queue_stats: SELECT aggregates; returns JSON stdout; exit 0 always
